cases.scope: Discovery (1123e, checkpoint sync off): the host dies by a native fall on Edge of the World; native GameOver "Restart From Last Checkpoint" issues RestartFromCheckpoint (kind 0), which caches the last autosave slot (61, the mission-start autosave), then RestartFromMemoryCheckpoint (kind 1) accepted for that slot.
1147: arm refused to pair: the client last autosave was still its Dunwall autosave (mission-start autosave not yet written) and the autosave write generation differed by timing -> 1147b.
cases.failure: Mission checkpoint arm failed host=awaiting_peer client=awaiting_peer

cases.scope: 1147b: armed after re-arm; shared death reached; restart aborted (host timeout, client peer_aborted) while the client sat at the load prompt; the harness pressed A on a shared timer and lost its timeline on failure. Cleanup could not disable the client session (load boundary pending); manual recovery: A on the client, sessions off, B out of pause, Recover-InterruptedTake (attempt 1 failed on the pause menu, kept as recovery-attempt1.json; attempt 2 passed).

Diagnostic rerun: shared death -> both native GameOver -> host restart -> both loading -> both held at the barrier -> released -> gameplay in about 8 s; each peer loaded its own slot 61 at its exact spawn; usable session renewed. Marked failed only by a cumulative count check that included 1149's abort.

Pass, two cycles: host death + host restart request, then client death + client restart request (the other peer presses as a duplicate). Each cycle: both native GameOver screens, exactly one load and one completion per peer, no abort, new world epochs, correct characters (1/2), exact mission-start spawn, usable session renewed after the shared checkpoint.

findings: Confirmed runtime (1146): on a mission, native GameOver restart = RestartFromCheckpoint -> last autosave slot (cached) -> memory continuation; each instance owns its own per-character autosaves.

Confirmed runtime (1151): mission checkpoint mode (1147b) turns either player's native death into a shared death (both native GameOver screens), deduplicates restart presses, and restarts each peer exactly once from its own mission autosave behind the existing both-ready barrier; usable sessions renew after the shared checkpoint.
Identity: autosave mapName/chapter/mission of the current map; arming waits for each peer's mission-start autosave.
outstanding: Mid-mission autosaves are per-player script events: a peer that crossed an autosave trigger alone holds a later checkpoint than the other (identity still matches by map). Pairing them needs the native RequestSave (slotType 3) issued on the peer when the host autosaves (hypothesis, not yet built).
